source_locator: R2225: ch. VII, Reinforcement by the 182d Infantry
current_activity: landing at Lunga Point as a regimental combat team, less 3rd Battalion
notes: Miller, ch. VII: Turner’s transports anchored off Lunga Point at 0530 on 12 November 1942 and landed the 182nd Regimental Combat Team, made up of the 1st and 2nd Battalions, 182nd Infantry, the 245th Field Artillery Battalion, and supporting troops (3,358 men). The 3rd Battalion was still in the New Hebrides. The caption dates the landing to 12 November. All about 6,000 troops on the ships debarked before the transports withdrew that evening. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. IX, General Patch Takes Command, as already cited on C12786 and C12821
current_activity: under Americal as Patch assumed command of troops ashore
notes: Inferred command change, same pattern as the 164th Infantry (C12821). Miller, chapter IX, dates Patch’s assumption of command of troops ashore to 9 December 1942, when the Americal Division headquarters took over from the 1st Marine Division. The 182nd had landed on 12 November while Vandegrift still commanded ashore. Confidence 0.5: inferred from that command change, not a separate 182nd location narrative.

location_qualifier: coastal line west of Point Cruz
source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, The CAM Division
current_activity: moving into the coastal line on the left of the 6th Marines, less 3rd Battalion
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: the 182nd Infantry (less the 3rd Battalion, then attached to the 35th Infantry) moved into line on the left of the 6th Marines on 17 January 1943, after Patch attached the 1st and 2nd Battalions to the 2nd Marine Division to form the CAM Division. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. The 3rd Battalion is not given a separate unit row.

location_qualifier: inland left of the coastal attack
source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, The CAM Division
current_activity: attacking on the CAM Division left and contacting the 25th Division
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: on 22 January 1943 the 182nd Infantry, on the left of the CAM Division, maintained contact with the 25th Division. By 1600 G Company of the 182nd had made contact with the 27th Infantry north of Hill 88. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal
current_activity: attacking inland and advancing about 1,000 yards beyond the Poha
notes: Miller, ch. XV: on 26 January 1943 the 182nd Infantry attacked on the high ground inland, abreast of the 6th Marines, as the CAM Division advanced 1,000 yards beyond the Poha. It met only stragglers and a few riflemen and machine gunners. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal

notes: Miller, ch. XV: on 29 January 1943 Patch detached the 147th Infantry from the CAM Division to pursue, and the 182nd Infantry then reverted to control of the Americal Division in the Lunga perimeter. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.
